Option helpers for as_widget()

Source: R/options.R
widget-options.Rd

These helpers group related as_widget() settings into one argument each:

Usage

tooltip_options(delay = 0, follow = TRUE, sticky = FALSE, style = NULL)

export_options(filename = "plot", scale = 1)

navigator_options(height = 56)

render_options(
  mode = c("auto", "svg", "raster"),
  raster_threshold = 20000L,
  text = c("native", "outline"),
  max_marks = 2000000L,
  detail_marks = 3000L,
  precision = c("compact", "f32"),
  max_zoom = 100,
  autoplay = TRUE,
  loop = TRUE
)

Arguments

delay

Milliseconds to wait before the tooltip appears on hover (default 0, i.e. immediate). The highlight is unaffected — only the tooltip waits. A short delay (e.g. 250) calms a dense scatter.

follow

When TRUE (default) the tooltip tracks the cursor; when FALSE it anchors above the hovered mark's centre.

sticky

When TRUE, the tooltip accepts pointer events and lingers briefly when you leave the mark, so you can move into it — for tooltips that contain links or buttons (build the HTML via tooltip = in the plot). Default FALSE.

style

Optional named list styling the tooltip box: background / color (any R or CSS colour), fontsize, and max_width (any CSS length; a bare number is used as is). NULL (default) uses the built-in style. Tooltip text is rendered as safe HTML — an author-built tooltip = (e.g. via glue()) may use <b>/<i>/<br> for bold/italic/line breaks; data values are escaped and only those inert tags are honoured (no scripts/attributes).

filename

The download filename base, without extension (default "plot").

scale

The PNG resolution multiplier (default 1). Exports capture the current (zoomed/panned) view.

height

Height of the navigator strip in pixels (default 56). Passing navigator_options() to as_widget(navigator = ) turns the navigator on; navigator = TRUE is the same as navigator = navigator_options().

mode

Rendering strategy for the marks. "auto" (default) ships a per-element SVG for small/moderate plots and switches to a single embedded raster image above raster_threshold keyed elements; "svg" always uses the per-element SVG; "raster" always uses the image. In raster mode the marks are drawn once as a base image and all interaction (hover, click, brush, pan/zoom) is driven client-side from the element index (geometry + boxes + keys), so a very large scatter (100k+ points) stays navigable with a tiny DOM and a small payload. With a vellum that has the split render (layer = on vellum::scene_svg()), only the keyed marks are an image: the axes, gridlines, legend and text stay SVG, so axis-aware zoom re-ticks the real axes, and the navigator and vellumplot::bind_scale() work as in SVG mode. With a vellum that also splits the furniture by paint order, what was drawn after the marks (a reference line or annotation added after the points) stays on top of them. An older vellum draws the whole scene as one image, and zoom then magnifies it. The trade-offs of raster mode: there are no per-element DOM nodes until the detail tier (see detail_marks), so hover and selection show as rings and per-mark screen-reader focus is off. Zoomed in, the marks are redrawn exactly from vellum's marks-only display list (see max_marks), or as plain dots with an older vellum. With the display list, vellumplot::condition() colours and dimming, vellumplot::filter_by(), cross-filters and legend hide/mute show at every zoom: the marks are then drawn on a canvas from the list. Without it (an older vellum, or more marks than max_marks), and for marks the list cannot reproduce (gradients, grouped marks), these show only in the detail tier.

raster_threshold

Keyed-element count above which mode = "auto" switches to the raster image (default 20000).

text

How text is written into the SVG, passed to vellum::scene_svg(): "native" (default) emits selectable <text> referencing system fonts — smaller when the page has the font, post-processable, and better for accessibility and LLMs; "outline" emits glyph outlines that are pixel-faithful and font-independent but not selectable. Applies to the SVG, including raster mode's SVG furniture under the split render; with an older vellum, raster mode bakes text into the base image and this argument is ignored (with a warning if set explicitly).

max_marks

In raster mode with a vellum that has the marks-only display list, the most marks whose exact geometry and paint ship with the widget (default 2000000). Zoomed-in marks are then redrawn exactly, with their own shape, colour, stroke and alpha. With precision = "compact" a scatter's widget takes about 6 MB per million points (1 million: 6.2 MB, 2 million: 12.2 MB, keys included) and about 5 s per million to build. Above it, the widget ships only a bounding-box index, about as big (6.3 MB per million), draws zoomed-in marks as plain dots (each in its own mark's colour), and says so with a message: a plot that big is better drawn as density, with vellumplot::mark_datashade() or vellumplot::mark_hex().

detail_marks

In raster mode with the display list, once a zoom settles with fewer than this many marks in view (default 3000), the visible marks become real SVG nodes (the detail tier): hover, selection, condition() and filter_by() styling and keyboard focus then work on them as in SVG mode. Zooming back out past 1.5 times this many returns to the canvas. 0 turns the detail tier off.

precision

How the display list ships its marks' coordinates (see max_marks). "compact" (default), with a vellum that supports it, quantises each coordinate column within its range so that no coordinate is off by more than 0.005 px, the precision of the SVG vellum writes (SVG mode, and raster mode's axes and gridlines): 16 bits per value for a plot up to 655 px across, 24 above, instead of a 32-bit float. That halves the coordinates in the payload (a 200k-point scatter: 2.7 to 1.7 MB) and keeps the error under half a pixel up to 100x zoom. "f32" ships 32-bit floats, as an older vellum always does.

max_zoom

The most the view zooms in, per axis, over the full view (default 100), in SVG and raster mode alike: the wheel, pinch, keys, box zoom and zoom-to-selection, vw_zoom(), linked views (group =) and vellumplot::bind_scale() all stop there. At 100x the 0.01 px grid vellum writes SVG coordinates on (and the 0.005 px error of precision = "compact") is still within half a screen pixel, so the marks stay on their gridlines; past it they drift (a few pixels at 1000x) and show only the rounding. A number from 1 (no zoom in) to 10000: past about 16,000x a 32-bit float can no longer place a mark at all.

autoplay, loop

For an animation (from vellumplot::animate()): whether it starts playing as soon as it is shown (default TRUE; FALSE starts paused on the first frame, for the reader to press play), and whether it loops (default TRUE; FALSE plays once and stops on the last frame, and pressing play there starts it over). A reader whose system asks for reduced motion always gets it paused. They need JavaScript: the animated SVG on its own always plays and loops. Ignored for a static plot.

Value

An object of class vellumwidget_tooltip_options, vellumwidget_export_options, vellumwidget_navigator_options or vellumwidget_render_options, to pass to the matching as_widget() argument.

Details

  • tooltip_options() for the hover tooltip (as_widget(tooltip = ));

  • export_options() for the toolbar's SVG/PNG download (as_widget(export = ));

  • navigator_options() for the overview range navigator (as_widget(navigator = ));

  • render_options() for how the marks are drawn (as_widget(render = )).

Each validates its arguments and returns an object that as_widget() reads. Calling a helper with no arguments gives the defaults.

Examples

tooltip_options(delay = 250, style = list(background = "#1d3557"))
#> <tooltip_options>
#>   delay: 250
#>   follow: TRUE
#>   sticky: FALSE
#>   style: list(background = #1d3557)
export_options(filename = "mtcars", scale = 2)
#> <export_options>
#>   filename: mtcars
#>   scale: 2
navigator_options(height = 80)
#> <navigator_options>
#>   height: 80
render_options(mode = "raster")
#> <render_options>
#>   mode: raster
#>   raster_threshold: 20000
#>   text: native
#>   max_marks: 2e+06
#>   detail_marks: 3000
#>   precision: compact
#>   max_zoom: 100
#>   autoplay: TRUE
#>   loop: TRUE

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(vellumplot)
vplot(mtcars) |>
  mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, tooltip = rownames(mtcars)) |>
  as_widget(
    tooltip = tooltip_options(delay = 250, follow = FALSE),
    export = export_options(filename = "mtcars", scale = 2)
  )
} # }
